project.title: From Scattered State to Authoritative Task Workflows
project.subtitle: Signal-driven loading and readiness for Pharmacy UI
project.positioning: Asynchronous task data needs one authoritative lifecycle owner, while each task keeps its own business-readiness rules.

format.visualDirection: Dark, diagram-led, and high-contrast with red for legacy risk, green for new ownership, and blue for UI outcomes

introduction.title: From scattered state to authoritative task workflows
introduction.subtitle: One loading model. Task-specific readiness. Predictable user experience.

legacy-problem.title: One task. Too many independent owners.
legacy-problem.subtitle: The UI can observe a workflow between updates—after some values arrive, but before the task is actually safe to use.

new-solution.title: Separate the lifecycles. Centralize the ownership.
new-solution.subtitle: Each open task gets one instance-scoped workflow store and three explicit responsibilities.

pickup-proof.title: Pick Up proves the pattern in production code.
pickup-proof.subtitle: The drawer owns stable patient groups and renders only authoritative task responses.

verify.title: Ready is not the same as actionable.
verify.subtitle: Verify has one authoritative data gate, followed by its task-specific readiness policy.
verify.failureOutcome: Incomplete or failed data → controlled error + Retry

fill-dispense.title: Two data gates. One final readiness decision.
fill-dispense.subtitle: Fill adds a medication-dispense dependency before its business rules can be evaluated.
fill-dispense.failureOutcome: Missing action or dispense IDs → visible not-ready / error state

outcomes.title: Common architecture. Task-specific rules.
outcomes.subtitle: The user always sees usable data, meaningful progress, or a clear path to recover.
